definition: A variable such as $a_{1}X_{1} + a_{2}X_{2} + \dots + a_{n}X_{n}$ built by multiplying random variables by constants and adding; its expected value is always the same combination of the expected values, while its variance is $a_{1}^{2}\mathrm{Var}(X_{1}) + \dots + a_{n}^{2}\mathrm{Var}(X_{n})$ only when the variables are independent, with every term added even for a difference.

The expected squared distance of a random variable from its mean, $\mathrm{Var}(X) = \mathrm{E}\left((X - \mu)^{2}\right)$, in squared units; for constants $a$ and $b$, $\mathrm{Var}(aX + b) = a^{2}\mathrm{Var}(X)$, so adding a constant does not change it.

An estimate of a population parameter whose expected value over all random samples of the same size equals that parameter, such as $\bar{x}$ for $\mu$ and $s_{n-1}^{2} = \frac{n}{n-1}s_{n}^{2}$ (dividing by $n - 1$, not $n$) for $\sigma^{2}$.
